authority_law: effective authority = authenticated principal ∩ tenant ∩ registered capability ∩ policy ∩ risk constraints ∩ required approval ∩ budget ∩ sandbox ∩ secret scope ∩ execution context

repositories.authority: declares and validates intent; never grants execution authority
owns workspace/session/task/workflow/lifecycle composition; never grants execution authority
transports typed requests and opaque authoritative results; never authorizes

repositories.role: sole governed execution and authority plane
repositories.authority: sole authority for identity, tenancy, authorization, policy, approvals, budgets, sandbox/tool authority, secrets, execution and authoritative evidence

gate.production_claims: must distinguish repository evidence from external deployment evidence

OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026: agent-specific adversarial risks
MCP 2026-07-28: authorization hardening, stateless transport and protocol evolution
A2A 1.0.x: authenticated agent discovery and horizontal agent collaboration

invariants: execution success is distinct from business outcome
Both replicas use the same four-repository contracts and versioned workforce profile.
Replica identifiers and tenant/workspace identifiers are unique.
Tenant isolation is mandatory and cannot be weakened by replication.
No replica identifier, catalog entry, model output, memory, tool output, or workflow declaration grants authority.
Platform remains the sole authority plane for both replicas.
Replication is parameterized; credentials, customer data, and provider secrets are never fixture data.
